Hi there, 

I'm struggling a bit with variogram interpretation, what are some useful references?

For example below- this bird has a small range and I would consider it range resident based on its behaviour- and yet I'd interpret the variogram as not reaching an asymptote? This is a fully zoomed out variogram, should interpretations be made based on a fully zoomed out variogram? 

My variograms look generally a lot more unstable than some of the other examples I've seen on this forum

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Variogram interpretation: useful references
parts:
Hi Christie,

In cases like this, I would hold judgement to compare the empirical variogram (here in black) versus the selected model's theoretical variogram (not shown here). If the two match fairly well for most of the initial variogram, where the CIs are narrow, then that's a good sign of residence. The tail end of the variogram has very large and very autocorrelated errors. But if the selected model's theoretical variogram is really high at the beginning (not matching the empirical variogram there) and you can see that it's matching at the end, which is also increasing like this, then that's a sign that there's some sort of shift or dispersal in the data.

Best,
Chris
